fact.claim: In 2026, taxable income from $58,523.01 to $107,785 is taxed at 20.5% federal plus 9.15% Ontario, for a combined marginal rate of 29.65%. If your taxable income is in that range both before and after the deduction, a $5,000 RRSP deduction lowers your tax by about $1,483. Other brackets get different amounts: about $1,158 at 23.15% (from $53,891.01 to $58,523), and Ontario's surtax and health premium can change the result for some incomes. The CRA's rule says the 2026 contribution year ends on the 60th day of 2027, which is Monday, March 1, 2027. The CRA has not posted that date on its own pages yet, and money contributed after that date can't be deducted on your 2026 return.

plain.what: An RRSP is a special account for retirement savings. Money you put in gets taken off your income at tax time, so you pay less tax. Put $5,000 in an RRSP, and if your taxable income sits between $58,523.01 and $107,785 in Ontario, your tax drops by about $1,483.
plain.so_what: That $1,483 is the gap between two coworkers who earn the same and both saved $5,000, and the only difference is which account the money sat in.
plain.do: Write down your taxable income and find which row it lands in before March 1, 2027.
